Source format: Maintenance manual

2.1 The press hall floor was prepared to the specification in drawing URB-2/68-001. The floor must be level to within 1.5 mm over any 3 m length, and the area marked out for the press must be swept clean of all debris and swarf before the first section is off-loaded. The concrete must have reached its full curing strength; this was verified by the civil contractor on 4th January 1968 and the certificate is filed with the building services office.

2.2 The following services were required and are to be confirmed present before commissioning:

- 3-phase electrical supply, 415 V, 50 Hz, with a separate earth bonding point.
- Compressed air line, 6 bar minimum, fitted with a water trap and pressure regulator.
- Water supply for the damping system, with a drain point nearby.
- Adequate lighting over the delivery end and the reel stand area.

2.3 The foundation bolts were set into the floor in accordance with the template supplied. Care was taken to ensure the bolts were held firmly in position while the concrete was poured; any movement of the bolts during the pour will cause misalignment that is difficult to correct later. The bolt positions were checked on 12th February 1968 and found to be within tolerance.

---

**Section 3: Delivery and Unloading**

3.1 The press arrived in eight road trailers between 18th and 21st February 1968. The delivery note was checked against the packing list, and all items were accounted for before any trailer was released. One crate (No. 4) had been damaged in transit; the contents were inspected and found to be the delivery end guard rails, which were scratched but not otherwise damaged. A claim was lodged with the haulier on 22nd February.

3.2 Unloading was carried out using the overhead crane rated at 10 tonnes. The heaviest single lift was the folder section, which weighed approximately 6.5 tonnes. Two slings were used, with a spreader bar to prevent damage to the top frame. The folder was placed directly onto the prepared floor at its final position, on timber packing pieces.

3.3 The sections were placed in the order of assembly, starting from the folder and working back towards the reel stand. This sequence is important; the sections must be placed so that the mating faces are accessible for bolting and alignment.

3.4 **NOTE:** The reel stand was delivered with the two arms in the raised position. Do not lower the arms until the stand is bolted down and the hydraulic oil has been added. Operating the arms without oil will damage the pump.

Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 installed_year 1968 year. Record status: historical.

---

**Section 4: Assembly and Alignment**

4.1 The sections were assembled in the following order:

1. Folder section.
2. Second printing unit (Unit 2).
3. First printing unit (Unit 1).
4. Reel stand.

4.2 The mating faces of each section were cleaned with a solvent to remove the protective grease applied at the factory. The faces were then checked for burrs or damage; any high spots were removed with a fine file. Do not use a grinder on the mating faces, as this will remove too much material and affect the alignment.

4.3 The sections were bolted together using the high-tensile bolts supplied. The bolts were tightened gradually, working from the centre of each joint outwards, to avoid distorting the frames. The final torque setting is given in Section 9.

4.4 Alignment of the press was carried out using a taut wire and a feeler gauge, following the procedure in drawing URB-2/68-004. The wire was set along the centre line of the press, and each section was adjusted until the distance from the wire to the side frames was equal on both sides. The tolerance is ±0.5 mm.

4.5 The folder section was aligned first, as it is the reference for the rest of the press. The printing units were then aligned to the folder, and the reel stand was aligned last. The reel stand is the least critical for side-to-side alignment, but it must be square to the press centre line to ensure the web runs true.

---
**Section 5: General Operating Parameters**

5.1 The press is designed for continuous operation at a web speed that will give the rated output, provided the paper, ink and blanket conditions are within the tolerances given in the appropriate sections of this manual. Operators should note that the figures quoted in this section are for the press as installed at this site, with the drive and gearing as supplied. Any alteration to the drive system, or the fitting of non-standard rollers, will invalidate these figures.

5.2 The following table gives the principal operating parameters for Press No. 2. The figures were checked on site during the commissioning run and are the figures to be used when setting the press for normal production.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Maximum rated speed | 25000 copies per hour | See note 5.2.1 below. |
| Normal running speed | 22000 copies per hour | For continuous running on newsprint. |
| Acceleration/deceleration rate | 5000 copies per hour per minute | Do not exceed this rate when starting or stopping the press. |
| Web width (max) | 1400 mm | As fitted at this site. |
| Cut-off | 578 mm | Two pages around. |
| Folder capacity | 2:1:1 jaw folder | Delivering single copy, quarter fold. |
| Reel stand capacity | 2 reels | Automatic paster. |

5.2.1 **NOTE ON MAXIMUM RATED SPEED:** According to the manual, the Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 maximum_rated_speed is 25000 copies per hour. Record status: current. This is the mechanical maximum of the press as designed, and is the figure used for all calculations of output and for the rating of the drive motor. It is not a running speed for continuous production. The press will run at this speed only for short periods, for example when making up time on a tight schedule, and then only with the paper, ink and blanket conditions at their best. The normal running speed of 22000 copies per hour is the speed for which the press was set up at commissioning and is the speed that should be used for all routine work. See also the warning in Section 5.3.

5.3 **WARNING:** DO NOT RUN THE PRESS ABOVE THE MAXIMUM RATED SPEED OF 25000 COPIES PER HOUR. The press is fitted with a mechanical overspeed trip which will stop the press if this speed is exceeded, but running at or near the maximum for long periods will cause excessive wear on the cylinder bearings (brgs) and on the folder cams. The overspeed trip is set at the factory and must not be adjusted on site. If the trip operates, the cause of the overspeed must be found and corrected before the press is restarted.

5.4 The press is driven by a variable speed DC motor, controlled from the main console. The speed is set by the operator using the hand wheel on the console, and the actual speed is shown on the tachometer. The tachometer is calibrated in copies per hour, and the reading should be checked against the job card before starting a run.

5.5 The press is fitted with a web tension control system which maintains a constant tension on the web between the reel stand and the first printing unit. The tension is set by a spring-loaded dancer roller, and the setting is adjusted by a hand wheel on the reel stand. The correct tension for a given paper is given in the paper suppliers’ data sheet, but a general guide is given in the table below.

| Paper weight (g/m²) | Tension setting (divisions on hand wheel) |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| 40 | 3 |
| 45 | 4 |
| 48.8 (newsprint) | 5 |
| 52 | 6 |

5.6 The folder is fitted with a tucker blade and jaw system, and the timing of the blade and jaws must be set correctly for the cut-off. The timing is set at commissioning and should not need adjustment unless the folder has been stripped down for maintenance. The procedure for setting the folder timing is given in Section 11.

**Section 6 — Cylinder Dimensions and Blanket Packing**

6.1 General

The following section gives the principal dimensions of the printing cylinders for both Press 1 and Press 2, together with the recommended blanket and underpacking for each unit. All dimensions are given in inches unless otherwise stated. Measurements are taken at the face of the cylinder, i.e. the outside diameter of the bearer ring, unless the text indicates otherwise.

The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 cylinder_circumference is listed as 22.5 inches. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry for all replacement parts and for setting the web cut-off. It is the value that is used in all subsequent calculations in this manual and on the Job Specification Sheets issued with each order.

6.2 Cylinder Data Table

The table below lists the cylinder dimensions for the two presses covered by this manual. These values are the current figures, as agreed at the last full survey of both machines (July 1985, Mr. D. Hargreaves). Any earlier figures appearing in the 1968 original edition are superseded by the values in this table.

| Item | Press 1 (Urbanite No. 1) | Press 2 (Urbanite No. 2) |
|------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| Plate cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Blanket cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Impression cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Plate cylinder bearer diameter (in) | 7.125 | 7.125 |
| Blanket cylinder bearer diameter (in) | 7.125 | 7.125 |
| Cylinder gap (degrees) | 90° | 90° |
| Plate thickness, standard (in) | 0.012 | 0.012 |
| Blanket thickness, standard (in) | 0.077 | 0.077 |

Note: The plate and blanket cylinders are of the same nominal circumference so that the plate can be changed without altering the web lead. The impression cylinder is of the same circumference to keep the printing nip evenly loaded. The bearer diameters are identical so that the nip can be set using feeler gauges between the bearers, as described in Section 6.4.

6.3 Blanket Packing

The correct packing of the blanket is essential for good print quality and for the life of the blanket. The packing must be checked whenever a new blanket is fitted, and at each routine service (every 500 hours running time, see Section 9).

The packing under the blanket is made up of a hard packing sheet (0.004 in) and one or more soft underpacking sheets (0.003 in each). The total packing must be such that the blanket surface stands 0.002 in proud of the bearer ring when the blanket is fitted and tensioned.

The following procedure is to be used:

1. Clean the blanket cylinder face with a lint-free cloth and a small amount of white spirit. Remove all old packing and any adhesive residue from the cylinder gap.
2. Lay the hard packing sheet in the cylinder gap first, with the cut-out for the gap register.
3. Lay the soft underpacking sheets on top of the hard sheet. Use only the number of sheets required to bring the blanket surface to the correct height. Do not use more than three soft sheets, as this will cause the blanket to be too soft and will result in a slurred print.
4. Fit the blanket over the packing, ensuring that the blanket bar is seated correctly in the gap.
5. Tension the blanket evenly, using the tensioning screws on the cylinder. The tension should be such that the blanket is firm but not drum-tight. A drum-tight blanket will cause excessive wear on the blanket cylinder bearers.
6. Check the height of the blanket surface using a dial gauge mounted on the press frame. The reading should be 0.002 in above the bearer ring, plus or minus 0.0005 in. If the reading is incorrect, slacken the blanket, adjust the packing, and re-tension.
7.2 Floor Loadings

The following loadings are for guidance only. The actual loading will depend on the
number of units, the reel stand, and the folder, and on the particular installation. The
figures given are for a four-unit press with a two-web folder, which is the most common
configuration.

| Item | Static load (kg) | Dynamic load (kg) |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| Each printing unit (complete with rollers) | 1,850 | 2,300 |
| Two-web folder (complete) | 2,400 | 3,100 |
| Reel stand (two reels, empty) | 900 | 1,200 |
| Reel stand (two reels, full) | 2,600 | 3,400 |

The dynamic load includes the effect of the impression nip and the inertia of the
cylinders when the press is running at speed. The floor must be capable of
withstanding the dynamic load without excessive deflection. A deflection of more than
0.5 mm under the drive side of the press will cause the drive shaft to be misaligned
and will result in a noisy drive and rapid wear of the universal joints.

7.3 Holding-Down Bolts

The press is supplied with holding-down bolts of the expanding type. These are suitable
for use in concrete floors of at least 150 mm thickness. For thinner floors, or for
floors of hollow-tile construction, use the alternative bolts supplied (see Parts List,
Section 14).

The holding-down bolts are positioned to suit the holes in the frame feet. The
positions are given in the dimensioned drawing URB/IC/2/D1, which is supplied with the
press. The drawing shows the position of each bolt relative to the centre line of the
press and to the drive side wall.

Before grouting in the bolts, check that the bolt positions are correct by lowering the
frame onto the bolts and checking that the bolts pass freely through the holes in the
frame feet. Do not force the frame onto the bolts. If the bolts are not in the correct
position, the frame will be pulled out of line when the nuts are tightened.

Goss Urbanite Press No. 1 installed_year 1954 year. Record status: historical.

7.4 Grouting

The frame feet are drilled and tapped for the holding-down bolts. The feet are also
provided with grout holes, through which grout is injected after the press has been
levelled and aligned.

The grout should be a non-shrink cementitious grout, mixed to a pourable consistency.
The grout should be poured through the grout holes until it appears at the edges of the
frame feet. The grout should be allowed to cure for at least 48 hours before the
holding-down bolts are finally tightened.

Do not tighten the holding-down bolts until the grout has fully cured. Tightening the
bolts onto uncured grout will cause the grout to crack and the press to settle unevenly.

7.5 Levelling and Alignment

The press is levelled using the adjusting screws provided at each frame foot. The
adjusting screws are accessible from the outside of the frame. Level the press in the
following order:

1. Level the drive side frame first, in both directions. Use a precision spirit level,
   placed on the machined surfaces of the frame, near the bearer housings.
2. Level the operating side frame, in both directions, relative to the drive side.
   Check the alignment of the two frames using a straight edge across the bearer
   housings, at both ends of the press.
3. Check the diagonals. The distance between the front bearer housing on the drive
   side and the rear bearer housing on the operating side should be equal to the
   distance between the rear bearer housing on the drive side and the front bearer
   housing on the operating side. If the diagonals are not equal, the press is
   out of square, and the frames must be adjusted before the grout is poured.

The press must be level to within 0.1 mm per metre, in both directions. This is
essential for the correct operation of the ink and water systems, and for the even
running of the folder.

8.3 Mechanical Checks

1. Check that the bearers are clean and free from rust. The bearers should be
   wiped with a clean, lint-free cloth, and lightly oiled with a thin machine oil.
2. Check that the cylinder settings are correct. The settings are given in
   Section 9 of this manual.
3. Check that the folder is correctly timed. The timing procedure is given in
   Section 10.
4. Check that all oil levels are correct. The oil levels should be checked with
   the press stopped, and the oil should be topped up if necessary. The oil
   grades and quantities are given in the Lubrication Chart, Section 11.
5. Check that the air supply is connected to the press, and that the air pressure
   is set to the value given in the installation drawings.
6. Check that the paper reel stands are correctly positioned and that the
   brakes are adjusted. The brakes should be adjusted so that the reel is held
   firmly when the brake is applied, but so that the reel can be turned by
   hand when the brake is released.

8.4 Checks on the Ink and Water Systems

1. Check that the ink ducts are clean and that the ink keys are free to move.
   The ink keys should be adjusted so that they are just touching the ink
   roller, and then backed off by half a turn.
2. Check that the water system is filled with water, and that the water
   circulates freely. The water should be a mixture of water and fountain
   solution, in the proportions given in the installation drawings.
3. Check that the water rollers are clean and that they are set correctly. The
   roller settings are given in Section 9.

SECTION 9 – CYLINDER SETTINGS

9.1 General

The cylinder settings are critical to the correct operation of the press. The
settings given in this section are for the standard newspaper format, as supplied
with the press. If the press is to be used for a different format, the settings must
be adjusted accordingly.

The settings are given in thousandths of an inch, and are measured between the
bearer surfaces, unless otherwise stated.

According to the manual, the Goss Urbanite Press No. 1 maximum_rated_speed is 18000 copies per hour. Record status: historical.

9.2 Plate Cylinder to Blanket Cylinder

The plate cylinder and the blanket cylinder should be set so that the bearers are
just touching, and then the plate cylinder is backed off by 0.004 inch. This gives
a printing pressure of 0.004 inch, which is suitable for most newspaper
applications.

Do not set the plate cylinder to blanket cylinder pressure to less than 0.002
inch, as this may result in poor ink transfer and a weak print.

9.3 Blanket Cylinder to Impression Cylinder

The blanket cylinder and the impression cylinder should be set so that the
bearers are just touching, and then the blanket cylinder is backed off by 0.003
inch. This gives a printing pressure of 0.003 inch.

The impression cylinder settings should be checked at both ends of the cylinder,
and the settings should be the same at both ends. If the settings are not the
same, the cylinder is not parallel to the blanket cylinder, and the press will
produce a print that is heavier on one side than the other.

9.4 Setting the Cylinders

To set the cylinders, proceed as follows:

1. Stop the press and isolate the electrical supply.
2. Remove the guards from the cylinder area.
3. Turn the press over by hand, using the inching button, until the cylinders
   are in the position shown in the installation drawings.
4. Loosen the lock nuts on the adjusting screws.
5. Turn the adjusting screws until the bearers are just touching. Use a feeler
   gauge to check that the bearers are touching evenly along their length.
6. Back off the adjusting screws by the amount given in Sections 9.2 and 9.3.
   Use a dial test indicator to measure the amount of back off.
7. Tighten the lock nuts, and check that the settings have not changed.
8. Replace the guards, and remove the padlock from the isolator.
**Section 10: Lubrication**

The correct and regular lubrication of the press is essential for its satisfactory operation and long life. The lubrication points, the type of lubricant to be used, and the frequency of lubrication are given in the following tables and in the Lubrication Chart (Drawing No. URB-1147, Sheet 3 of 4).

WARNING: DO NOT OPERATE THE PRESS UNLESS ALL LUBRICATION POINTS HAVE BEEN FILLED WITH THE CORRECT LUBRICANT. OPERATING THE PRESS WITHOUT LUBRICATION WILL CAUSE SERIOUS DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS AND GEARS.

The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 lubrication_oil_type is Goss Spec 220. Record status: current. This specification has been current since the press was commissioned and remains the required grade for all circulating oil systems on the press. No substitute grade is approved without the written authorisation of Goss International.

**10.1 Circulating Oil Systems (Units 1 to 4)**

Each printing unit is fitted with a self-contained circulating oil system. The system comprises a sump, a pump, a filter, and a distribution manifold which feeds oil to the cylinder bearings, the gear train, and the auxiliary drive bearings.

The oil sump capacity for each unit is 18 litres (4 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked daily, with the press stopped, using the sight glass on the side of the sump. The level should be maintained between the HIGH and LOW marks.

The oil filter element should be cleaned after the first 100 hours of operation, and thereafter at intervals of 500 hours. To clean the filter, remove the bowl, wash the element in a suitable solvent, and allow it to dry before refitting. A blocked filter will cause a drop in oil pressure and may result in bearing failure.

The oil pressure should be checked at the gauge on the unit frame. The normal operating pressure is between 1.0 and 1.5 bar (15 to 22 psi) when the press is running at normal speed. If the pressure falls below 0.7 bar (10 psi), stop the press immediately and investigate the cause.

An oil pressure switch is fitted to each unit. This switch will stop the press automatically if the oil pressure falls below a safe level. The switch setting should be checked at each service, and the operation of the switch should be tested weekly by closing the isolating valve on the pump delivery line and observing that the press stops.

**10.2 Oil Change Intervals**

The oil in the circulating systems should be changed at the following intervals:

| Application | Interval |
|-------------|----------|
| Printing units (all) | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |
| Folder | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |
| Roller and dampener drive gearboxes | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |

When changing the oil, drain the sump while the oil is warm. Flush the system with a light flushing oil or with Goss Spec 220, then drain again. Refill with clean Goss Spec 220. Record the oil change in the maintenance log, noting the date, the hours run, and the initials of the engineer.

**10.3 Manual Lubrication Points**

The following points require manual lubrication with a grease gun or oil can. The frequency of lubrication is given in the table. Use a lithium-based grease (Goss Spec 110) for grease points, and Goss Spec 220 for oil points.

Wipe off any excess grease or oil after lubrication. Excess lubricant can attract dust and paper dust, which may cause wear or blockages.

**10.4 Folder Lubrication**

The folder gearbox is fitted with a separate oil sump. The sump capacity is 12 litres (2.6 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked weekly, and the oil should be changed at the same interval as the unit sumps (Section 10.2).
When changing the oil, remove the drain plug on the underside of the gearbox. Allow the oil to drain fully. Clean the magnetic drain plug before refitting. Refill with 1.5 litres (0.33 imperial gallons) of Goss Spec 220.

**10.9 Folder Gearbox**

The folder gearbox is fitted with a separate oil sump. The sump capacity is 12 litres (2.6 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked weekly, and the oil should be changed at the same interval as the unit sumps (Section 10.2).

The folder gearbox is fitted with a magnetic drain plug. Clean the plug at each oil change. The gearbox breather should be cleaned annually.

**10.10 Grease Points**

All grease points should be lubricated with Goss Spec 110 (lithium-based grease). The following table lists the grease points and their frequencies. Wipe off any excess grease after lubrication.

| Grease Point | Frequency |
|--------------|-----------|
| Unit cam rollers | Weekly |
| Folder former board adjusters | Weekly |
| Folder tape rollers | Weekly |
| Angle bar rollers | Weekly |
| Paster brush rollers | Weekly |
| Roller and dampener drive universal joints | Monthly |
| Folder tucking knife pivot | Monthly |
| Folder jaw cam followers | Monthly |
| Delivery gripper bar cam followers | Monthly |
| Unit blanket cylinder bearers | 2,000 hours |

**10.11 Oil Change Intervals (Press No. 2)**

For Press No. 2 only, the following revised oil change intervals apply. These intervals supersede the general intervals in Section 10.2 for this press. The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 oil_change_interval is 500 operating hours. Record status: current. This interval is current and applies to all units, the folder, and the roller and dampener drive gearboxes on Press No. 2. The reduced interval was introduced following a review of oil analysis results from Press No. 2 in late 1987. The review found accelerated degradation of the oil in the unit sumps, attributed to the higher running speeds and increased web tensions at which Press No. 2 operates.

| Application | Interval (Press No. 2) |
|-------------|------------------------|
| Printing units (all) | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |
| Folder | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |
| Roller and dampener drive gearboxes | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |

The procedure for changing the oil is the same as given in Section 10.2. Drain the sump while the oil is warm. Flush the system with a light flushing oil or with Goss Spec 220, then drain again. Refill with clean Goss Spec 220. Record the oil change in the maintenance log, noting the date, the hours run, and the initials of the engineer.

The oil in the bearing housings (Section 10.7) and the folder gearbox (Section 10.9) on Press No. 2 should also be changed at the 500 hour interval.

**10.12 Hydraulic System (Press No. 2)**

The hydraulic power pack on Press No. 2 is the same as that described in Section 10.5. The return-line filter element should be replaced every 500 hours on this press, in line with the revised oil change interval. The reservoir should be topped up with Goss Spec 220 as required. Check the reservoir level fortnightly.

**10.13 Cold Weather Operation**

In cold weather, the oil in the circulating systems may become viscous. If the press is started from cold, allow the oil to circulate for at least 15 minutes before running the press at speed. The oil pressure may be higher than normal when the oil is cold. Do not adjust the pressure relief valve to compensate for cold oil. The oil will warm up as the press runs.

If the press is to be shut down for a prolonged period in cold weather, consider running the oil pumps for 30 minutes before shutdown to distribute warm oil through the system. This will help to prevent condensation forming in the sumps.

**13. COMMON OPERATIONAL PROBLEMS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

The following notes have been collected from running reports, engineers' job cards and
telephone call records. They are not exhaustive. Where a fault appears on only one
machine, the press number is stated. If no press number is given, the fault has been
seen on both Press 1 and Press 2.

**13.1 Paper Feed – Intermittent Misses**

**Symptom:** Sheets fail to reach the front lays at regular or irregular intervals. The
pile may appear level, but the side guide marks show a ragged edge.

**Cause A – Worn feed roller brgs.** The feed roller bearings wear and allow the roller
to lift, losing grip on the sheet.

**Action:**
1. Stop the press and lock out.
2. Remove the feed roller assembly.
3. Check the bearings for play by rocking the roller in its housing. Any perceptible
   movement means replacement.
4. Order replacement bearings stating Press No. 1 or Press No. 2. The bearing spec
   for Press No. 2 was revised in 1986; the two presses are not identical in this
   respect.
5. Re-fit, set the roller down on the pile with light even pressure, and re-check the
   side guide marks at slow speed before running.

**Cause B – Air blast too weak or mis-aimed.** The separator nozzles may be blocked
with paper dust.

**Action:**
1. Clean the nozzle tips with a stiff brush. Do not use wire.
2. Check the air pressure gauge at the pump. It should hold between 25 and 30 psi.
3. If the gauge drops when the blast valve opens, trace for a split hose or a loose
   jubilee clip.

**Cause C – Pile height control.** The pile may be running too low, so the feed roller
cannot pick up.

**Action:**
1. Check the pile height probe. It should ride on the back edge of the pile, not the
   centre.
2. If the probe is bent, straighten or replace (Part No. GU-2017).
3. Re-set the pile height so that the feed roller penetrates the pile by 1/8 in. to
   3/16 in.

**13.2 Ink Roller Streaking**

**Symptom:** A dark band appears across the sheet, parallel to the cylinder axis.
Usually on one side of the sheet only.

**Cause A – Form roller not parallel.** The roller may be set heavier at one end.

**Action:**
1. Stop the press.
2. Ink up the rollers and run a test plate at slow speed.
3. Stop the press and examine the ink stripe on the form roller. The stripe should be
   even across the full width.
4. If the stripe is wider at one end, slacken the locking nut on that end and adjust
   the eccentric bush. Re-tighten and re-test.
5. If the stripe cannot be made even, check the roller stock for a flat or a bulge.
   A roller that has been left standing on its face will take a flat and must be
   re-ground or replaced.

**Cause B – Vibrator roller glazed.** A glazed vibrator will not carry ink evenly.

**Action:**
1. Remove the vibrator roller.
2. Wash with the recommended solvent, then scrub with a fine pumice block.
3. If the glaze will not come off, the roller must be re-ground. This is a specialist
   job and should be sent out.

**13.3 Dampening Problems – Scumming**

**Symptom:** Non-image areas pick up ink, usually at the tail edge of the sheet.

**Cause A – Dampener form roller not touching the plate.** The roller may have been
set too light, or the stock has worn.

**Action:**
1. Check the dampener form roller setting against the plate. It should have a
   contact stripe of 3/16 in.
2. If the stripe is too thin, re-set the roller.
3. If the stripe is correct but the roller is shiny, the stock is worn or glazed.
   Replace the stock. See Section 12.5 for part numbers.

**Cause B – Metering roller setting.** The metering roller may be set too far from the
form roller, so the water film is too thick.
**13.4 Washing Up Between Runs**

The wash-up procedure is given here in full because a bad wash-up is the cause of
more lost production than any other single fault on the press. It is false economy
to hurry it.

1. Stop the press and trip the impression.
2. Run the wash-up brush over the form rollers. Use the recommended solvent
   (see Section 3.4). Do not use paraffin, diesel oil or any substitute.
3. Let the press run for 30 seconds to distribute the solvent.
4. Apply the wash-up blade. Run the press for not more than 2 minutes.
5. Remove the blade and allow the rollers to dry for 1 minute.
6. Wipe the plate cylinder and the blanket cylinder with a clean cotton rag.
   Do not use the same rag for both.
7. Check the dampening rollers for ink carry-over. If the stock is stained,
   wash it in the sink with warm water and a little detergent, then rinse
   thoroughly. Hang the stock to dry, do not wring it.
8. Clean the ink fountain and the fountain keys with the brass brush. Do not
   scrape the fountain with a steel spatula.

**WARNING:** THE WASH-UP BLADE IS SHARP. ALWAYS FIT THE GUARD BEFORE
STARTING THE PRESS. NEVER REACH OVER THE ROLLERS WHILE THE PRESS IS
RUNNING.

**13.5 Blanket Washing**

A clean blanket is essential for a good print. Wash the blanket at least once
per shift, and more often if the paper is dusty or the ink is heavy.

1. Trip the impression and stop the press.
2. Apply the blanket wash with a rag, working from the gripper edge to the
   tail edge. Do not rub in circles.
3. If the blanket has a glaze, use the pumice block, then wash again with the
   solvent.
4. Check the blanket for cuts, especially at the leading edge. A cut blanket
   will mark the sheet. Replace if the cut is deeper than 0.005 in.
5. Re-fit the blanket and tension it evenly. Over-tension will bow the cylinder.

**Note:** A blanket that has been left with ink on it overnight will take a
permanent glaze. This is not covered by warranty. See the warranty terms in
Section 1.7.

**13.6 Plate Changing**

The plate is held in position by the plate clamps at the leading and trailing
edges. The clamps are adjusted at the factory and should not be re-set unless
the plate is slipping.

1. Stop the press and trip the impression.
2. Release the leading edge clamp.
3. Pull the plate clear of the cylinder, taking care not to scratch the surface.
4. Slide the new plate into the leading edge clamp. Push it up to the stops.
5. Tighten the leading edge clamp, then the trailing edge clamp.
6. Run the press slowly and check the plate is square. If it is not square,
   slacken the trailing edge clamp and tap the plate gently.

**WARNING:** DO NOT USE A KNIFE OR A SCREWDRIVER TO PRY THE PLATE OFF THE
CYLINDER. THIS WILL DAMAGE THE CYLINDER BEARINGS.

**13.7 Blanket and Plate Packing**

The correct packing is given in the table below. The figures are for the
standard blanket and plate supplied by Goss. If you use a different make,
re-check the packing.

| Cylinder | Packing under blanket | Packing under plate |
|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Press 1  | 0.015 in.            | 0.004 in.           |
| Press 2  | 0.015 in.            | 0.004 in.           |

The packing is fitted in the gap at the cylinder undercut. Use only the
official packing sheets, Part No. GU-2031 (blanket) and GU-2032 (plate).
Do not use newspaper or card as a substitute.

**13.8 Roller Settings**

The roller settings are given in Section 12.4 and are repeated here for
convenience. The settings are taken with the press cold.

| Roller | Setting (contact stripe) |
|--------|--------------------------|
| Form rollers to plate | 3/16 in. |
| Form rollers to vibrator | 1/8 in. |
| Dampener form roller to plate | 3/16 in. |
| Dampener form roller to metering roller | 1/16 in. |

Maintenance log

MERROWBRIDGE PRINTWORKS — PRESS MAINTENANCE LOG
Book 2: Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 (Press 2)
Covering: January 1987 – December 1987

Entries recorded by shift engineers. Initials in margin denote the engineer responsible. Part numbers quoted where available from stores. Any entry marked “ARCHIVED” is a historical record and is not to be used for current planning.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 14 Feb 1987
SHIFT: Day
ENGINEER: D. Hargreaves (DH)
TIME IN: 07:40
TIME OUT: 16:05

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Replaced both sets of cylinder bearings on the main impression unit (brgs, both sides). Bearings had been running hot since the 9th; noise noted by operator on the morning of the 11th. Stripped the unit down on the 13th after the evening run and found the offside bearing cage starting to break up. Nearside bearing showed scoring on the rollers, likely from debris carried over.

– Fitted new bearings: SKF 22316 E (x2) – stores issue no. 4471. Also replaced the oil seals on the same housing (part no. MW-2214, x2) as the old ones were perished and letting oil weep onto the floor.

– Re-checked the nip setting on the impression cylinder after reassembly. Set to factory spec (0.10 mm crush) and ran a test sheet at 08:50. No vibration. Took the press up to 12,000 iph for a 10-minute run – temperature within normal range throughout.

– Noted that the folder section’s cam follower on the chopper blade is showing wear. Recommend replacement within the next 2-3 weeks. Not urgent but will need doing before the Easter schedule. Advised shift manager; stores to order cam follower (part no. MW-3310).

PARTS USED:
SKF 22316 E bearing (x2) – from stores
MW-2214 oil seal (x2) – from stores

REMARKS:
Press ran clean after the bearing change. The offside bearing that failed was the one replaced in May 1985 (see log entry 12 May 1985 – ARCHIVED). The near side had not been changed at that time, which was an oversight; both should always be done together to avoid uneven wear. This has been noted in the maintenance schedule for future reference.

The maintenance log records that Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 bearings_replaced_on 1987-02-14. Record status: historical.

Signed: D. Hargreaves (DH)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 16 Feb 1987
SHIFT: Day
ENGINEER: P. Okafor (PO)
TIME IN: 08:00
TIME OUT: 17:10

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Follow-up check on the bearing replacement carried out on 14 Feb. Ran the press at full speed for 30 minutes with the folder engaged. Checked bearing housing temperature with the infra-red gun – offside reading 48°C, nearside 51°C. Both within acceptable range.

– Topped up the oil in the main gearbox (grade 220) – approx. 2 litres.

– Investigated a slight rattle from the reel stand area. Found that the tension arm pivot pin (part no. MW-1187) had worked loose. Tightened and lockwired. Will monitor.

REMARKS:
No further issues. The bearing replacement appears to have resolved the overheating.

Signed: P. Okafor (PO)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 20 Feb 1987
SHIFT: Night
ENGINEER: T. Whitfield (TW)
TIME IN: 22:00
TIME OUT: 06:30

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Press stopped at 01:15 with a paper jam in the folder. Cleared the jam and found that the chopper blade had nicked the paper on the previous run – likely due to the worn cam follower noted by DH on 14 Feb. The blade itself is still serviceable but the cam follower should be replaced as a priority.

– Checked the cam follower – confirmed wear on the contact face. Part is on order (MW-3310) but has not arrived yet. Spoke to stores – they are chasing the supplier.
DATE: 27 Feb 1987
SHIFT: Day
ENGINEER: D. Hargreaves (DH)
TIME IN: 08:15
TIME OUT: 16:45

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Cam follower (MW-3310) arrived from stores this morning. Fitted to the folder unit. Checked the contact face against the cam – full contact across the face, no rocking. The old follower was badly worn on the outer edge; this would have caused the chopper blade to sit slightly out of line, which is what nicked the paper on the 20 Feb run.

– Re-set the chopper blade clearance to spec (0.08mm – 0.10mm feeler gauge). Checked the blade for damage – the nick from 20 Feb has not affected the cutting edge. Blade can stay in service for now.

– Ran the folder at slow speed for 15 minutes, then at full speed for 20 minutes. No further nicking, fold quality good.

REMARKS:
The folder is back to normal. The cam follower that failed was last replaced in March 1984 (see log entry 14 Mar 1984 – ARCHIVED). That was just under three years ago, which is a bit short for this part; the supplier has changed the material spec on the new ones, so hopefully they will last longer. The maintenance schedule has been updated to check the cam follower at every 6-month service rather than annually.

Signed: D. Hargreaves (DH)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 03 Mar 1987
SHIFT: Night
ENGINEER: P. Okafor (PO)
TIME IN: 22:00
TIME OUT: 06:20

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Routine night check of Press 2. All oil levels OK. Bearing housing temperatures on the folder and the main drum within normal range (44°C – 52°C).

– Noticed a small oil weep on the folder cam housing. Traced it to the seal on the cam shaft (part no. MW-2214 – same as used on the main drum). The seal is not leaking badly, but it has softened and is starting to weep. Will need replacing soon. The seal was fitted in November 1986, so it has only been in service about four months. This is the same batch of seals that gave trouble on Press 1 last year – see log entry 09 Sep 1986. I have flagged this to DH.

– Topped up the folder cam housing with oil (grade 68) – approx. 0.5 litre.

REMARKS:
No other issues. The press ran steadily all night. I have left a note for the day shift to order a replacement seal (MW-2214) so we have one in stock when we do the change.

Signed: P. Okafor (PO)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 06 Mar 1987
SHIFT: Day
ENGINEER: T. Whitfield (TW)
TIME IN: 08:00
TIME OUT: 16:30

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Replaced the cam shaft seal (MW-2214) on the folder. The old seal had indeed softened – the lip had lost its tension and was riding slightly out of the groove. Cleaned the housing and fitted the new seal with a thin film of grease on the lip. Reassembled and ran the folder for 10 minutes – no weep.

– Also checked the tension arm pivot pin (MW-1187) that PO tightened on 16 Feb. Still tight, lockwire intact. No movement.

– Greased the reel stand tension arms (2 nipples) and the folder cam follower pivot (1 nipple).

REMARKS:
The seal failure is the same batch problem as noted on Press 1. I have checked the stores bin – there are two more MW-2214 seals left from that batch. I would suggest we do not use them and ask the supplier for a fresh batch, or at least have them inspected before fitting. I have put a note in the stores requisition book.

Signed: T. Whitfield (TW)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
DATE: 10 Mar 1987
SHIFT: Day
ENGINEER: D. Hargreaves (DH)
TIME IN: 07:45
TIME OUT: 17:00

WORK CARRIED OUT:

– Spoke to the supplier about the MW-2214 seals. They admit there was a bad batch in late 1986 – the rubber compound was not cured properly. They are sending a replacement batch free of charge, due in by the end of the month. The two remaining seals from the bad batch have been pulled from stores and set aside – they will not be used.

documents.content:
2.1 The press hall floor was prepared to the specification in drawing URB-2/68-001. The floor must be level to within 1.5 mm over any 3 m length, and the area marked out for the press must be swept clean of all debris and swarf before the first section is off-loaded. The concrete must have reached its full curing strength; this was verified by the civil contractor on 4th January 1968 and the certificate is filed with the building services office.

2.2 The following services were required and are to be confirmed present before commissioning:

- 3-phase electrical supply, 415 V, 50 Hz, with a separate earth bonding point.
- Compressed air line, 6 bar minimum, fitted with a water trap and pressure regulator.
- Water supply for the damping system, with a drain point nearby.
- Adequate lighting over the delivery end and the reel stand area.

2.3 The foundation bolts were set into the floor in accordance with the template supplied. Care was taken to ensure the bolts were held firmly in position while the concrete was poured; any movement of the bolts during the pour will cause misalignment that is difficult to correct later. The bolt positions were checked on 12th February 1968 and found to be within tolerance.

---

**Section 3: Delivery and Unloading**

3.1 The press arrived in eight road trailers between 18th and 21st February 1968. The delivery note was checked against the packing list, and all items were accounted for before any trailer was released. One crate (No. 4) had been damaged in transit; the contents were inspected and found to be the delivery end guard rails, which were scratched but not otherwise damaged. A claim was lodged with the haulier on 22nd February.

3.2 Unloading was carried out using the overhead crane rated at 10 tonnes. The heaviest single lift was the folder section, which weighed approximately 6.5 tonnes. Two slings were used, with a spreader bar to prevent damage to the top frame. The folder was placed directly onto the prepared floor at its final position, on timber packing pieces.

3.3 The sections were placed in the order of assembly, starting from the folder and working back towards the reel stand. This sequence is important; the sections must be placed so that the mating faces are accessible for bolting and alignment.

3.4 **NOTE:** The reel stand was delivered with the two arms in the raised position. Do not lower the arms until the stand is bolted down and the hydraulic oil has been added. Operating the arms without oil will damage the pump.

Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 installed_year 1968 year. Record status: historical.

---

**Section 4: Assembly and Alignment**

4.1 The sections were assembled in the following order:

1. Folder section.
2. Second printing unit (Unit 2).
3. First printing unit (Unit 1).
4. Reel stand.

4.2 The mating faces of each section were cleaned with a solvent to remove the protective grease applied at the factory. The faces were then checked for burrs or damage; any high spots were removed with a fine file. Do not use a grinder on the mating faces, as this will remove too much material and affect the alignment.

4.3 The sections were bolted together using the high-tensile bolts supplied. The bolts were tightened gradually, working from the centre of each joint outwards, to avoid distorting the frames. The final torque setting is given in Section 9.

4.4 Alignment of the press was carried out using a taut wire and a feeler gauge, following the procedure in drawing URB-2/68-004. The wire was set along the centre line of the press, and each section was adjusted until the distance from the wire to the side frames was equal on both sides. The tolerance is ±0.5 mm.

4.5 The folder section was aligned first, as it is the reference for the rest of the press. The printing units were then aligned to the folder, and the reel stand was aligned last. The reel stand is the least critical for side-to-side alignment, but it must be square to the press centre line to ensure the web runs true.

---

**Section 5: General Operating Parameters**

5.1 The press is designed for continuous operation at a web speed that will give the rated output, provided the paper, ink and blanket conditions are within the tolerances given in the appropriate sections of this manual. Operators should note that the figures quoted in this section are for the press as installed at this site, with the drive and gearing as supplied. Any alteration to the drive system, or the fitting of non-standard rollers, will invalidate these figures.

5.2 The following table gives the principal operating parameters for Press No. 2. The figures were checked on site during the commissioning run and are the figures to be used when setting the press for normal production.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Maximum rated speed | 25000 copies per hour | See note 5.2.1 below. |
| Normal running speed | 22000 copies per hour | For continuous running on newsprint. |
| Acceleration/deceleration rate | 5000 copies per hour per minute | Do not exceed this rate when starting or stopping the press. |
| Web width (max) | 1400 mm | As fitted at this site. |
| Cut-off | 578 mm | Two pages around. |
| Folder capacity | 2:1:1 jaw folder | Delivering single copy, quarter fold. |
| Reel stand capacity | 2 reels | Automatic paster. |

5.2.1 **NOTE ON MAXIMUM RATED SPEED:** According to the manual, the Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 maximum_rated_speed is 25000 copies per hour. Record status: current. This is the mechanical maximum of the press as designed, and is the figure used for all calculations of output and for the rating of the drive motor. It is not a running speed for continuous production. The press will run at this speed only for short periods, for example when making up time on a tight schedule, and then only with the paper, ink and blanket conditions at their best. The normal running speed of 22000 copies per hour is the speed for which the press was set up at commissioning and is the speed that should be used for all routine work. See also the warning in Section 5.3.

5.3 **WARNING:** DO NOT RUN THE PRESS ABOVE THE MAXIMUM RATED SPEED OF 25000 COPIES PER HOUR. The press is fitted with a mechanical overspeed trip which will stop the press if this speed is exceeded, but running at or near the maximum for long periods will cause excessive wear on the cylinder bearings (brgs) and on the folder cams. The overspeed trip is set at the factory and must not be adjusted on site. If the trip operates, the cause of the overspeed must be found and corrected before the press is restarted.

5.4 The press is driven by a variable speed DC motor, controlled from the main console. The speed is set by the operator using the hand wheel on the console, and the actual speed is shown on the tachometer. The tachometer is calibrated in copies per hour, and the reading should be checked against the job card before starting a run.

5.5 The press is fitted with a web tension control system which maintains a constant tension on the web between the reel stand and the first printing unit. The tension is set by a spring-loaded dancer roller, and the setting is adjusted by a hand wheel on the reel stand. The correct tension for a given paper is given in the paper suppliers’ data sheet, but a general guide is given in the table below.

| Paper weight (g/m²) | Tension setting (divisions on hand wheel) |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| 40 | 3 |
| 45 | 4 |
| 48.8 (newsprint) | 5 |
| 52 | 6 |

5.6 The folder is fitted with a tucker blade and jaw system, and the timing of the blade and jaws must be set correctly for the cut-off. The timing is set at commissioning and should not need adjustment unless the folder has been stripped down for maintenance. The procedure for setting the folder timing is given in Section 11.

**Section 6 — Cylinder Dimensions and Blanket Packing**

6.1 General

The following section gives the principal dimensions of the printing cylinders for both Press 1 and Press 2, together with the recommended blanket and underpacking for each unit. All dimensions are given in inches unless otherwise stated. Measurements are taken at the face of the cylinder, i.e. the outside diameter of the bearer ring, unless the text indicates otherwise.

The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 cylinder_circumference is listed as 22.5 inches. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry for all replacement parts and for setting the web cut-off. It is the value that is used in all subsequent calculations in this manual and on the Job Specification Sheets issued with each order.

6.2 Cylinder Data Table

The table below lists the cylinder dimensions for the two presses covered by this manual. These values are the current figures, as agreed at the last full survey of both machines (July 1985, Mr. D. Hargreaves). Any earlier figures appearing in the 1968 original edition are superseded by the values in this table.

| Item | Press 1 (Urbanite No. 1) | Press 2 (Urbanite No. 2) |
|------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| Plate cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Blanket cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Impression cylinder circumference (in) | 22.5 | 22.5 |
| Plate cylinder bearer diameter (in) | 7.125 | 7.125 |
| Blanket cylinder bearer diameter (in) | 7.125 | 7.125 |
| Cylinder gap (degrees) | 90° | 90° |
| Plate thickness, standard (in) | 0.012 | 0.012 |
| Blanket thickness, standard (in) | 0.077 | 0.077 |

Note: The plate and blanket cylinders are of the same nominal circumference so that the plate can be changed without altering the web lead. The impression cylinder is of the same circumference to keep the printing nip evenly loaded. The bearer diameters are identical so that the nip can be set using feeler gauges between the bearers, as described in Section 6.4.

6.3 Blanket Packing

The correct packing of the blanket is essential for good print quality and for the life of the blanket. The packing must be checked whenever a new blanket is fitted, and at each routine service (every 500 hours running time, see Section 9).

The packing under the blanket is made up of a hard packing sheet (0.004 in) and one or more soft underpacking sheets (0.003 in each). The total packing must be such that the blanket surface stands 0.002 in proud of the bearer ring when the blanket is fitted and tensioned.

The following procedure is to be used:

1. Clean the blanket cylinder face with a lint-free cloth and a small amount of white spirit. Remove all old packing and any adhesive residue from the cylinder gap.
2. Lay the hard packing sheet in the cylinder gap first, with the cut-out for the gap register.
3. Lay the soft underpacking sheets on top of the hard sheet. Use only the number of sheets required to bring the blanket surface to the correct height. Do not use more than three soft sheets, as this will cause the blanket to be too soft and will result in a slurred print.
4. Fit the blanket over the packing, ensuring that the blanket bar is seated correctly in the gap.
5. Tension the blanket evenly, using the tensioning screws on the cylinder. The tension should be such that the blanket is firm but not drum-tight. A drum-tight blanket will cause excessive wear on the blanket cylinder bearers.
6. Check the height of the blanket surface using a dial gauge mounted on the press frame. The reading should be 0.002 in above the bearer ring, plus or minus 0.0005 in. If the reading is incorrect, slacken the blanket, adjust the packing, and re-tension.

7.2 Floor Loadings

The following loadings are for guidance only. The actual loading will depend on the
number of units, the reel stand, and the folder, and on the particular installation. The
figures given are for a four-unit press with a two-web folder, which is the most common
configuration.

| Item | Static load (kg) | Dynamic load (kg) |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| Each printing unit (complete with rollers) | 1,850 | 2,300 |
| Two-web folder (complete) | 2,400 | 3,100 |
| Reel stand (two reels, empty) | 900 | 1,200 |
| Reel stand (two reels, full) | 2,600 | 3,400 |

The dynamic load includes the effect of the impression nip and the inertia of the
cylinders when the press is running at speed. The floor must be capable of
withstanding the dynamic load without excessive deflection. A deflection of more than
0.5 mm under the drive side of the press will cause the drive shaft to be misaligned
and will result in a noisy drive and rapid wear of the universal joints.

7.3 Holding-Down Bolts

The press is supplied with holding-down bolts of the expanding type. These are suitable
for use in concrete floors of at least 150 mm thickness. For thinner floors, or for
floors of hollow-tile construction, use the alternative bolts supplied (see Parts List,
Section 14).

The holding-down bolts are positioned to suit the holes in the frame feet. The
positions are given in the dimensioned drawing URB/IC/2/D1, which is supplied with the
press. The drawing shows the position of each bolt relative to the centre line of the
press and to the drive side wall.

Before grouting in the bolts, check that the bolt positions are correct by lowering the
frame onto the bolts and checking that the bolts pass freely through the holes in the
frame feet. Do not force the frame onto the bolts. If the bolts are not in the correct
position, the frame will be pulled out of line when the nuts are tightened.

Goss Urbanite Press No. 1 installed_year 1954 year. Record status: historical.

7.4 Grouting

The frame feet are drilled and tapped for the holding-down bolts. The feet are also
provided with grout holes, through which grout is injected after the press has been
levelled and aligned.

The grout should be a non-shrink cementitious grout, mixed to a pourable consistency.
The grout should be poured through the grout holes until it appears at the edges of the
frame feet. The grout should be allowed to cure for at least 48 hours before the
holding-down bolts are finally tightened.

Do not tighten the holding-down bolts until the grout has fully cured. Tightening the
bolts onto uncured grout will cause the grout to crack and the press to settle unevenly.

7.5 Levelling and Alignment

The press is levelled using the adjusting screws provided at each frame foot. The
adjusting screws are accessible from the outside of the frame. Level the press in the
following order:

1. Level the drive side frame first, in both directions. Use a precision spirit level,
   placed on the machined surfaces of the frame, near the bearer housings.
2. Level the operating side frame, in both directions, relative to the drive side.
   Check the alignment of the two frames using a straight edge across the bearer
   housings, at both ends of the press.
3. Check the diagonals. The distance between the front bearer housing on the drive
   side and the rear bearer housing on the operating side should be equal to the
   distance between the rear bearer housing on the drive side and the front bearer
   housing on the operating side. If the diagonals are not equal, the press is
   out of square, and the frames must be adjusted before the grout is poured.

The press must be level to within 0.1 mm per metre, in both directions. This is
essential for the correct operation of the ink and water systems, and for the even
running of the folder.

8.3 Mechanical Checks

1. Check that the bearers are clean and free from rust. The bearers should be
   wiped with a clean, lint-free cloth, and lightly oiled with a thin machine oil.
2. Check that the cylinder settings are correct. The settings are given in
   Section 9 of this manual.
3. Check that the folder is correctly timed. The timing procedure is given in
   Section 10.
4. Check that all oil levels are correct. The oil levels should be checked with
   the press stopped, and the oil should be topped up if necessary. The oil
   grades and quantities are given in the Lubrication Chart, Section 11.
5. Check that the air supply is connected to the press, and that the air pressure
   is set to the value given in the installation drawings.
6. Check that the paper reel stands are correctly positioned and that the
   brakes are adjusted. The brakes should be adjusted so that the reel is held
   firmly when the brake is applied, but so that the reel can be turned by
   hand when the brake is released.

8.4 Checks on the Ink and Water Systems

1. Check that the ink ducts are clean and that the ink keys are free to move.
   The ink keys should be adjusted so that they are just touching the ink
   roller, and then backed off by half a turn.
2. Check that the water system is filled with water, and that the water
   circulates freely. The water should be a mixture of water and fountain
   solution, in the proportions given in the installation drawings.
3. Check that the water rollers are clean and that they are set correctly. The
   roller settings are given in Section 9.

SECTION 9 – CYLINDER SETTINGS

9.1 General

The cylinder settings are critical to the correct operation of the press. The
settings given in this section are for the standard newspaper format, as supplied
with the press. If the press is to be used for a different format, the settings must
be adjusted accordingly.

The settings are given in thousandths of an inch, and are measured between the
bearer surfaces, unless otherwise stated.

According to the manual, the Goss Urbanite Press No. 1 maximum_rated_speed is 18000 copies per hour. Record status: historical.

9.2 Plate Cylinder to Blanket Cylinder

The plate cylinder and the blanket cylinder should be set so that the bearers are
just touching, and then the plate cylinder is backed off by 0.004 inch. This gives
a printing pressure of 0.004 inch, which is suitable for most newspaper
applications.

Do not set the plate cylinder to blanket cylinder pressure to less than 0.002
inch, as this may result in poor ink transfer and a weak print.

9.3 Blanket Cylinder to Impression Cylinder

The blanket cylinder and the impression cylinder should be set so that the
bearers are just touching, and then the blanket cylinder is backed off by 0.003
inch. This gives a printing pressure of 0.003 inch.

The impression cylinder settings should be checked at both ends of the cylinder,
and the settings should be the same at both ends. If the settings are not the
same, the cylinder is not parallel to the blanket cylinder, and the press will
produce a print that is heavier on one side than the other.

9.4 Setting the Cylinders

To set the cylinders, proceed as follows:

1. Stop the press and isolate the electrical supply.
2. Remove the guards from the cylinder area.
3. Turn the press over by hand, using the inching button, until the cylinders
   are in the position shown in the installation drawings.
4. Loosen the lock nuts on the adjusting screws.
5. Turn the adjusting screws until the bearers are just touching. Use a feeler
   gauge to check that the bearers are touching evenly along their length.
6. Back off the adjusting screws by the amount given in Sections 9.2 and 9.3.
   Use a dial test indicator to measure the amount of back off.
7. Tighten the lock nuts, and check that the settings have not changed.
8. Replace the guards, and remove the padlock from the isolator.

**Section 10: Lubrication**

The correct and regular lubrication of the press is essential for its satisfactory operation and long life. The lubrication points, the type of lubricant to be used, and the frequency of lubrication are given in the following tables and in the Lubrication Chart (Drawing No. URB-1147, Sheet 3 of 4).

WARNING: DO NOT OPERATE THE PRESS UNLESS ALL LUBRICATION POINTS HAVE BEEN FILLED WITH THE CORRECT LUBRICANT. OPERATING THE PRESS WITHOUT LUBRICATION WILL CAUSE SERIOUS DAMAGE TO THE BEARINGS AND GEARS.

The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 lubrication_oil_type is Goss Spec 220. Record status: current. This specification has been current since the press was commissioned and remains the required grade for all circulating oil systems on the press. No substitute grade is approved without the written authorisation of Goss International.

**10.1 Circulating Oil Systems (Units 1 to 4)**

Each printing unit is fitted with a self-contained circulating oil system. The system comprises a sump, a pump, a filter, and a distribution manifold which feeds oil to the cylinder bearings, the gear train, and the auxiliary drive bearings.

The oil sump capacity for each unit is 18 litres (4 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked daily, with the press stopped, using the sight glass on the side of the sump. The level should be maintained between the HIGH and LOW marks.

The oil filter element should be cleaned after the first 100 hours of operation, and thereafter at intervals of 500 hours. To clean the filter, remove the bowl, wash the element in a suitable solvent, and allow it to dry before refitting. A blocked filter will cause a drop in oil pressure and may result in bearing failure.

The oil pressure should be checked at the gauge on the unit frame. The normal operating pressure is between 1.0 and 1.5 bar (15 to 22 psi) when the press is running at normal speed. If the pressure falls below 0.7 bar (10 psi), stop the press immediately and investigate the cause.

An oil pressure switch is fitted to each unit. This switch will stop the press automatically if the oil pressure falls below a safe level. The switch setting should be checked at each service, and the operation of the switch should be tested weekly by closing the isolating valve on the pump delivery line and observing that the press stops.

**10.2 Oil Change Intervals**

The oil in the circulating systems should be changed at the following intervals:

| Application | Interval |
|-------------|----------|
| Printing units (all) | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |
| Folder | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |
| Roller and dampener drive gearboxes | Every 2,000 hours or 6 months, whichever comes first |

When changing the oil, drain the sump while the oil is warm. Flush the system with a light flushing oil or with Goss Spec 220, then drain again. Refill with clean Goss Spec 220. Record the oil change in the maintenance log, noting the date, the hours run, and the initials of the engineer.

**10.3 Manual Lubrication Points**

The following points require manual lubrication with a grease gun or oil can. The frequency of lubrication is given in the table. Use a lithium-based grease (Goss Spec 110) for grease points, and Goss Spec 220 for oil points.

Wipe off any excess grease or oil after lubrication. Excess lubricant can attract dust and paper dust, which may cause wear or blockages.

**10.4 Folder Lubrication**

The folder gearbox is fitted with a separate oil sump. The sump capacity is 12 litres (2.6 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked weekly, and the oil should be changed at the same interval as the unit sumps (Section 10.2).

**10.9 Folder Gearbox**

The folder gearbox is fitted with a separate oil sump. The sump capacity is 12 litres (2.6 imperial gallons). The recommended oil is Goss Spec 220. The oil level should be checked weekly, and the oil should be changed at the same interval as the unit sumps (Section 10.2).

The folder gearbox is fitted with a magnetic drain plug. Clean the plug at each oil change. The gearbox breather should be cleaned annually.

**10.10 Grease Points**

All grease points should be lubricated with Goss Spec 110 (lithium-based grease). The following table lists the grease points and their frequencies. Wipe off any excess grease after lubrication.

| Grease Point | Frequency |
|--------------|-----------|

| Folder former board adjusters | Weekly |
| Folder tape rollers | Weekly |
| Angle bar rollers | Weekly |
| Paster brush rollers | Weekly |
| Roller and dampener drive universal joints | Monthly |
| Folder tucking knife pivot | Monthly |
| Folder jaw cam followers | Monthly |
| Delivery gripper bar cam followers | Monthly |
| Unit blanket cylinder bearers | 2,000 hours |

**10.11 Oil Change Intervals (Press No. 2)**

For Press No. 2 only, the following revised oil change intervals apply. These intervals supersede the general intervals in Section 10.2 for this press. The Goss Urbanite Press No. 2 oil_change_interval is 500 operating hours. Record status: current. This interval is current and applies to all units, the folder, and the roller and dampener drive gearboxes on Press No. 2. The reduced interval was introduced following a review of oil analysis results from Press No. 2 in late 1987. The review found accelerated degradation of the oil in the unit sumps, attributed to the higher running speeds and increased web tensions at which Press No. 2 operates.

| Application | Interval (Press No. 2) |
|-------------|------------------------|
| Printing units (all) | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |
| Folder | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |
| Roller and dampener drive gearboxes | Every 500 hours or 3 months, whichever comes first |

The procedure for changing the oil is the same as given in Section 10.2. Drain the sump while the oil is warm. Flush the system with a light flushing oil or with Goss Spec 220, then drain again. Refill with clean Goss Spec 220. Record the oil change in the maintenance log, noting the date, the hours run, and the initials of the engineer.

The oil in the bearing housings (Section 10.7) and the folder gearbox (Section 10.9) on Press No. 2 should also be changed at the 500 hour interval.

**10.12 Hydraulic System (Press No. 2)**

The hydraulic power pack on Press No. 2 is the same as that described in Section 10.5. The return-line filter element should be replaced every 500 hours on this press, in line with the revised oil change interval. The reservoir should be topped up with Goss Spec 220 as required. Check the reservoir level fortnightly.

**10.13 Cold Weather Operation**

In cold weather, the oil in the circulating systems may become viscous. If the press is started from cold, allow the oil to circulate for at least 15 minutes before running the press at speed. The oil pressure may be higher than normal when the oil is cold. Do not adjust the pressure relief valve to compensate for cold oil. The oil will warm up as the press runs.

If the press is to be shut down for a prolonged period in cold weather, consider running the oil pumps for 30 minutes before shutdown to distribute warm oil through the system. This will help to prevent condensation forming in the sumps.

**13. COMMON OPERATIONAL PROBLEMS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS**

The following notes have been collected from running reports, engineers' job cards and
telephone call records. They are not exhaustive. Where a fault appears on only one
machine, the press number is stated. If no press number is given, the fault has been
seen on both Press 1 and Press 2.

**13.1 Paper Feed – Intermittent Misses**

**Symptom:** Sheets fail to reach the front lays at regular or irregular intervals. The
pile may appear level, but the side guide marks show a ragged edge.

**Cause A – Worn feed roller brgs.** The feed roller bearings wear and allow the roller
to lift, losing grip on the sheet.

**Action:**
1. Stop the press and lock out.
2. Remove the feed roller assembly.
3. Check the bearings for play by rocking the roller in its housing. Any perceptible
   movement means replacement.
4. Order replacement bearings stating Press No. 1 or Press No. 2. The bearing spec
   for Press No. 2 was revised in 1986; the two presses are not identical in this
   respect.
5. Re-fit, set the roller down on the pile with light even pressure, and re-check the
   side guide marks at slow speed before running.

**Cause B – Air blast too weak or mis-aimed.** The separator nozzles may be blocked
with paper dust.

**Action:**
1. Clean the nozzle tips with a stiff brush. Do not use wire.
2. Check the air pressure gauge at the pump. It should hold between 25 and 30 psi.
3. If the gauge drops when the blast valve opens, trace for a split hose or a loose
   jubilee clip.

**Cause C – Pile height control.** The pile may be running too low, so the feed roller
cannot pick up.

**Action:**
1. Check the pile height probe. It should ride on the back edge of the pile, not the
   centre.
2. If the probe is bent, straighten or replace (Part No. GU-2017).
3. Re-set the pile height so that the feed roller penetrates the pile by 1/8 in. to
   3/16 in.

**13.2 Ink Roller Streaking**

**Symptom:** A dark band appears across the sheet, parallel to the cylinder axis.
Usually on one side of the sheet only.

**Cause A – Form roller not parallel.** The roller may be set heavier at one end.

**Action:**
1. Stop the press.
2. Ink up the rollers and run a test plate at slow speed.
3. Stop the press and examine the ink stripe on the form roller. The stripe should be
   even across the full width.
4. If the stripe is wider at one end, slacken the locking nut on that end and adjust
   the eccentric bush. Re-tighten and re-test.
5. If the stripe cannot be made even, check the roller stock for a flat or a bulge.
   A roller that has been left standing on its face will take a flat and must be
   re-ground or replaced.

**Cause B – Vibrator roller glazed.** A glazed vibrator will not carry ink evenly.

**Action:**
1. Remove the vibrator roller.
2. Wash with the recommended solvent, then scrub with a fine pumice block.
3. If the glaze will not come off, the roller must be re-ground. This is a specialist
   job and should be sent out.

**13.3 Dampening Problems – Scumming**

**Symptom:** Non-image areas pick up ink, usually at the tail edge of the sheet.

**Cause A – Dampener form roller not touching the plate.** The roller may have been
set too light, or the stock has worn.

**Action:**
1. Check the dampener form roller setting against the plate. It should have a
   contact stripe of 3/16 in.
2. If the stripe is too thin, re-set the roller.
3. If the stripe is correct but the roller is shiny, the stock is worn or glazed.
   Replace the stock. See Section 12.5 for part numbers.

**Cause B – Metering roller setting.** The metering roller may be set too far from the
form roller, so the water film is too thick.

documents.content:
**13.4 Washing Up Between Runs**

The wash-up procedure is given here in full because a bad wash-up is the cause of
more lost production than any other single fault on the press. It is false economy
to hurry it.

1. Stop the press and trip the impression.
2. Run the wash-up brush over the form rollers. Use the recommended solvent
   (see Section 3.4). Do not use paraffin, diesel oil or any substitute.
3. Let the press run for 30 seconds to distribute the solvent.
4. Apply the wash-up blade. Run the press for not more than 2 minutes.
5. Remove the blade and allow the rollers to dry for 1 minute.
6. Wipe the plate cylinder and the blanket cylinder with a clean cotton rag.
   Do not use the same rag for both.
7. Check the dampening rollers for ink carry-over. If the stock is stained,
   wash it in the sink with warm water and a little detergent, then rinse
   thoroughly. Hang the stock to dry, do not wring it.
8. Clean the ink fountain and the fountain keys with the brass brush. Do not
   scrape the fountain with a steel spatula.

**WARNING:** THE WASH-UP BLADE IS SHARP. ALWAYS FIT THE GUARD BEFORE
STARTING THE PRESS. NEVER REACH OVER THE ROLLERS WHILE THE PRESS IS
RUNNING.

**13.5 Blanket Washing**

A clean blanket is essential for a good print. Wash the blanket at least once
per shift, and more often if the paper is dusty or the ink is heavy.

1. Trip the impression and stop the press.
2. Apply the blanket wash with a rag, working from the gripper edge to the
   tail edge. Do not rub in circles.
3. If the blanket has a glaze, use the pumice block, then wash again with the
   solvent.
4. Check the blanket for cuts, especially at the leading edge. A cut blanket
   will mark the sheet. Replace if the cut is deeper than 0.005 in.
5. Re-fit the blanket and tension it evenly. Over-tension will bow the cylinder.

**Note:** A blanket that has been left with ink on it overnight will take a
permanent glaze. This is not covered by warranty. See the warranty terms in
Section 1.7.

**13.6 Plate Changing**

The plate is held in position by the plate clamps at the leading and trailing
edges. The clamps are adjusted at the factory and should not be re-set unless
the plate is slipping.

1. Stop the press and trip the impression.
2. Release the leading edge clamp.
3. Pull the plate clear of the cylinder, taking care not to scratch the surface.
4. Slide the new plate into the leading edge clamp. Push it up to the stops.
5. Tighten the leading edge clamp, then the trailing edge clamp.
6. Run the press slowly and check the plate is square. If it is not square,
   slacken the trailing edge clamp and tap the plate gently.

**WARNING:** DO NOT USE A KNIFE OR A SCREWDRIVER TO PRY THE PLATE OFF THE
CYLINDER. THIS WILL DAMAGE THE CYLINDER BEARINGS.

**13.7 Blanket and Plate Packing**

The correct packing is given in the table below. The figures are for the
standard blanket and plate supplied by Goss. If you use a different make,
re-check the packing.

| Cylinder | Packing under blanket | Packing under plate |
|----------|----------------------|---------------------|

Do not use newspaper or card as a substitute.

documents.content:
**APPENDIX B — REFERENCE DATA**

**B.1 General Dimensions and Weights**

The following figures are for a standard Urbanite press with two units, one folder, and a
quarter-fold attachment. They are given for planning purposes only and should not be used
for structural calculations. Where a figure is critical, consult the works drawing (see
list in Section 1.4).

| Item | Dimension |
|------|-----------|
| Overall length, two units with folder | 42 ft 6 in. |
| Overall width, including platforms | 8 ft 3 in. |
| Height to top of folder | 6 ft 9 in. |
| Floor space required (recommended minimum) | 45 ft × 10 ft |
| Weight, complete as above | 11.5 tons |
| Weight, single unit | 3.4 tons |

Weights are dry weights, without ink, paper, or packing. Add 10% if the press is
fitted with a reeler stand.

**B.2 Air Consumption**

The press consumes air for the folder, the air bars (if fitted), and the blanket
washing device. Consumption is measured at 80 psi.

| Item | Consumption |
|------|-------------|
| Folder, normal running | 8 cfm |
| Folder, during changeover | 14 cfm |
| Air bars, per bar | 2.5 cfm |
| Blanket washing device | 6 cfm |

The compressor should be sized for the maximum simultaneous demand. A receiver
of at least 20 gallons is recommended. Pipe runs over 50 ft should be increased by
one pipe size.

**B.3 Water and Dampening**

The Urbanite standard dampening system uses a recirculating water supply. The
water should be treated with a fountain solution concentrate at the rate given on the
bottle. Never use untreated water for more than one shift.

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Water temperature (recommended) | 10–15 °C |
| pH (as mixed) | 4.5–5.5 |
| Alcohol substitute (if used) | 10% by volume |

If the water is hard (over 200 ppm), a water softener should be fitted. Scale
deposits on the metering roller are not covered by warranty.

**B.4 Electrical Supply**

The press is supplied for a 415 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz supply unless otherwise ordered.
The main isolator is fitted at the drive side of unit 1.

| Item | Rating |
|------|--------|
| Main drive motor | 15 hp |
| Folder motor | 5 hp |
| Pump motors (each) | 0.5 hp |
| Total connected load | approx. 22 kVA |
| Recommended fuse size | 60 A per phase |

The earth continuity conductor must be at least 4 mm². The press must be earthed
in accordance with the current IEE Regulations. If the supply voltage varies by more
than 5%, the drive may trip. Check the supply before commissioning.

**B.5 Lubrication Chart**

The lubrication points are marked on the press with red paint discs. The chart below
is a summary; full details are in Section 9.

| Point | Lubricant | Interval |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| Form roller bearings | Shell Alvania 2 | Weekly |
| Vibrator bearings | Shell Alvania 2 | Weekly |
| Cylinder gears | Shell Omala 220 | Monthly |
| Folder gears | Shell Omala 220 | Monthly |
| Delivery chain | Shell Tonna 68 | Daily |
| Air bar swivels | Shell Alvania 2 | Monthly |

Use a grease gun with a hydraulic adapter. Do not over-grease; two strokes of the
gun is sufficient. Excess grease can work its way onto the paper and cause marking.

**B.6 Spare Parts List (Recommended Initial Stock)**

The following parts should be held in stock for the first year of operation. The
quantities are for a single press. For a two-press installation, increase the quantity
by 50% for the wearing items.
